class=\"num\">.114 [.079, .154]</td>\n            <td class=\"num\">.870 [.822, .909]</td>\n            <td class=\"num\">.027 [.007, .053]</td>\n          </tr>\n        </tbody>\n      </table>\n    </div>\n\n    <p>\n      <strong>GaMS3:</strong> abliteration removes refusal almost completely in both languages.\n      English refusal drops from 98.6% to 1.4%; Slovene from 87.1% to 0.0%. The edit transfers fully.\n      <a href=\"https://github.com/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-beaa2a-what-english-tuned-abliteration-misses/tree/main/round-2/experiment-6\">Code: What English edits miss in Slovene: GaMS3 panel.</a>\n    </p>\n    <p>\n      <strong>Gemma:</strong> abliteration partially suppresses English refusal\n      (97.1% to 28.7%) but barely affects Slovene (93.9% to 73.9%).\n      The English ASR reaches 73.8%, far below GaMS3's 98.2%; Slovene ASR is 10.3%.\n      <a href=\"https://github.com/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-beaa2a-what-english-tuned-abliteration-misses/tree/main/round-2/experiment-7\">Code: English edits barely unlock Slovene refusal in Gemma.</a>\n    </p>\n    <p>\n      <strong>Community reference:</strong> the independently abliterated Gemma achieves much lower refusal in both English (5.4%) and Slovene (11.4%), suggesting that a more thorough abliteration procedure can reach deeper into the refusal mechanism.\n      <a href=\"https://github.com/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-beaa2a-what-english-tuned-abliteration-misses/tree/main/round-1/experiment-1\">Code: Same edit, very different safety effect.</a>\n    </p>\n\n    <h3>Keyword measurement bias</h3>\n\n    <div class=\"result-highlight\">\n      <span class=\"big-num\">&Delta;<sub>lang</sub> = &minus;1.56</span>\n      The keyword counter fires on 87% of English responses but 0% of Slovene responses.\n      The reference judge finds 13% English refusal and 82% Slovene refusal.\n      95% CI [&minus;1.68, &minus;1.44].\n    </div>\n\n    <p>\n      The keyword refusal counter counts English refusal phrases (\"I cannot\", \"I'm sorry\", etc.)\n      in model responses. It is structurally unable to detect Slovene refusals.\n      The threshold-blind fraction (TBF) is 1.0 in both searches: every candidate that\n      a scorer places at or below the selection threshold (&le; 10/100 refusals) is invisible\n      to the keyword objective. Under scorer C, 6/6 Gemma and 37/37 GaMS3 candidates are\n      invisible; under the reference judge J, 5/5 and 6/6.\n      <a href=\"https://github.com/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-beaa2a-what-english-tuned-abliteration-misses/tree/main/round-5/evaluation-5\">Code: How blind is an English-only refusal score.</a>\n    </p>\n\n    <div class=\"table-wrap\">\n      <table>\n        <caption class=\"sr-only\">Keyword refusal counter vs. judge reference on held-out prompts.</caption>\n        <thead>\n          <tr>\n            <th>Condition</th><th>n</th><th>&kappa;</th><th>KW pos. rate</th><th>Ref. base rate</th><th>Mechanism</th>\n          </tr>\n        </thead>\n        <tbody>\n          <tr><td>Original EN</td><td class=\"num\">70</td><td class=\"num\">0.20</td><td class=\"num\">0.94</td><td class=\"num\">0.94</td><td>CONCORDANT</td></tr>\n          <tr><td>Original SL</td><td class=\"num\">70</td><td class=\"num\">0.00</td><td class=\"num\">0.00</td><td class=\"num\">0.96</td><td>SILENT</td></tr>\n          <tr><td>Edited EN</td><td class=\"num\">490</td><td class=\"num\">0.02</td><td class=\"num\">0.34</td><td class=\"num\">0.17</td><td>MISFIRING</td></tr>\n          <tr><td>Edited SL</td><td class=\"num\">490</td><td class=\"num\">0.00</td><td class=\"num\">0.00</td><td class=\"num\">0.44</td><td>SILENT</td></tr>\n        </tbody>\n      </table>\n    </div>\n\n    <p>\n      On Slovene text the keyword counter produces zero positives regardless of whether the model\n      refuses (0/490 held-out Slovene responses flagged). On edited English text, 81.4% of its\n      detections are false positives, and its &kappa; against the judge is 0.02.\n      <a href=\"https://github.com/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-beaa2a-what-english-tuned-abliteration-misses/tree/main/round-4/experiment-15\">Code: Can a refusal optimiser see its own refusals?</a>\n    </p>\n\n    <h3>Depth placement vs. dose</h3>\n\n    <p>\n      Heretic treats which layers to edit and the scaling coefficient as free parameters.\n      We construct causal write profiles by applying single-layer abliteration edits in\n      isolation.\n      <a href=\"https://github.com/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-beaa2a-what-english-tuned-abliteration-misses/tree/main/round-4/experiment-13\">Code: Where a refusal edit lands decides what survives.</a>\n    </p>\n\n    <p>\n      For Gemma, Spearman correlations between depth-placement index and residual refusal are\n      &rho; = &minus;0.96 for English and &rho; = &minus;0.83 for Slovene (n = 18 weight cells).\n      For GaMS3, &rho; = &minus;0.90 (Slovene, p &lt; 10<sup>&minus;7</sup>),\n      holding at both energy levels (&rho; = &minus;0.97 at E2, &rho; = &minus;0.95 at E3).\n      <a href=\"https://github.com/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-beaa2a-what-english-tuned-abliteration-misses/tree/main/round-4/experiment-14\">Code: Where a refusal edit must land in a Slovene model.</a>\n    </p>\n\n    <p>\n      Across 42 matched pairs in the Gemma experiment (energy-matched, varying layer identity),\n      placements targeting depth-peak layers leave lower Slovene refusal than off-peak\n      placements of equal energy (mean &Delta;<sub>SL</sub> = 0.12, 95% CI [0.07, 0.18]).\n      English refusal is approximately invariant to placement at matched energy\n      (mean &Delta;<sub>EN</sub> = 0.006).\n    </p>\n\n    <div class=\"result-highlight\">\n      <span class=\"big-num\">&rho; = &minus;0.009</span>\n      Cross-model prediction fails entirely. The activation-space depth index does not transfer\n      between Gemma and Qwen3-8B (n = 21, p = 0.16).\n      <a href=\"https://github.com/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-beaa2a-what-english-tuned-abliteration-misses/tree/main/round-3/experiment-12\">Code: Depth index fails to predict cross-lingual refusal-edit failure.</a>\n    </div>\n  </section>\n\n  <!-- ============ FIGURES ============ -->\n  <section id=\"figures\">\n    <h2>Figures</h2>\n    <div class=\"figure-gallery\">\n\n      <figure class=\"figure-item\">\n        <div class=\"fig-img-wrap\" role=\"button\" tabindex=\"0\" aria-label=\"Enlarge figure: Refusal Rates Before and After Abliteration\" data-src=\"figures/fig_1_v0.png\">\n          <img src=\"figures/fig_1_v0.png\" alt=\"Bar chart showing refusal rates on RefusEU S5 harmful prompts for five checkpoints in English and Slovene. GaMS3 edit drops to near zero in both languages, while Gemma edit drops only in English, remaining at 73.9% in Slovene.\" loading=\"lazy\">\n        </div>\n        <figcaption>\n          <strong>Figure 1: Refusal Rates Before and After Abliteration.</strong>\n          Refusal rates on RefusEU S5 harmful prompts (n=280) for all five checkpoints in English\n          and Slovene. Abliteration transfers almost completely to Slovene for GaMS3 (orange) but\n          fails for Gemma (blue). The community reference checkpoint (grey) shows that deeper\n          abliteration can partially overcome the language gap. Error bars show 95% Clopper-Pearson\n          confidence intervals. Note: 94-95% of edited English outputs were truncated at the\n          256-token generation limit.\n        </figcaption>\n      </figure>\n\n      <figure class=\"figure-item\">\n        <div class=\"fig-img-wrap\" role=\"button\" tabindex=\"0\" aria-label=\"Enlarge figure: Keyword Measurement Bias\" data-src=\"figures/fig_2_v0.png\">\n          <img src=\"figures/fig_2_v0.png\" alt=\"Side-by-side bar charts comparing keyword counter vs reference judge positive rates. The keyword counter fires on 87% of English but 0% of Slovene responses; the reference judge finds 13% English and 82% Slovene refusal.\" loading=\"lazy\">\n        </div>\n        <figcaption>\n          <strong>Figure 2: Keyword Measurement Bias.</strong>\n          Keyword counter vs. reference judge positive rates for the Gemma-edit checkpoint on 100\n          verified paired prompts. The keyword counter fires on 87% of English responses but 0% of\n          Slovene responses; the reference judge finds 13% English refusal and 82% Slovene refusal.\n          &Delta;<sub>lang</sub> = &minus;1.56 [&minus;1.68, &minus;1.44]. The keyword counter is\n          structurally blind to Slovene refusals.\n        </figcaption>\n      </figure>\n\n      <figure class=\"figure-item\">\n        <div class=\"fig-img-wrap\" role=\"button\" tabindex=\"0\" aria-label=\"Enlarge figure: Depth Placement Profile for GaMS3\" data-src=\"figures/fig_3_v0.png\">\n          <img src=\"figures/fig_3_v0.png\" alt=\"Scatter plot of residual Slovene refusal rate as a function of write-profile overlap for GaMS3, showing strong negative correlation (Spearman rho minus 0.90). Points are shown at two energy levels, E2 and E3.\" loading=\"lazy\">\n        </div>\n        <figcaption>\n          <strong>Figure 3: Depth Placement Profile for GaMS3.</strong>\n          Residual Slovene refusal rate as a function of depth placement for GaMS3-12B-Instruct.\n          Each point is a single abliteration configuration; the x-axis is a depth-placement index\n          (lower = shallower layers). Spearman &rho; = &minus;0.90 (p &lt; 10<sup>&minus;7</sup>).\n          Deeper placements produce lower residual Slovene refusal. The relationship holds within\n          both energy levels (E2: &rho; = &minus;0.97; E3: &rho; = &minus;0.95).\n        </figcaption>\n      </figure>\n\n    </div>\n  </section>\n\n  <!-- ============ LIMITATIONS ============ -->\n  <section id=\"limitations\">\n    <h2>Limitations</h2>\n    <ul class=\"limitations-list\">\n      <li>\n        <strong>Slovene judge certification.</strong> The Qwen3-14B workhorse judge does not meet\n        the &kappa; &ge; 0.80 certification gate for Slovene (unweighted &kappa; = 0.72,\n        CI [0.63, 0.81]). Absolute Slovene refusal rates may be biased. Within-Slovene relative\n        comparisons are less affected, since the bias is approximately constant across checkpoints.\n      </li>\n      <li>\n        <strong>Generation truncation.</strong> 94-95% of edited English outputs and 70-92% of\n        edited Slovene outputs were truncated at the 256-token generation limit. The judge classified\n        refusal status from incomplete text.\n      </li>\n      <li>\n        <strong>Two models, one architecture.</strong> Both models are closely related (Gemma and\n        its continual-pretraining derivative). The Qwen3-8B cross-model test provides one additional\n        architecture, but a systematic survey across model families is needed.\n      </li>\n      <li>\n        <strong>One target language.</strong> Slovene is a mid-resource Indo-European language.\n        The keyword measurement bias extends to any language the keyword counter does not cover,\n        but the degree of edit transfer failure may differ for typologically distant or extremely\n        low-resource languages.\n      </li>\n      <li>\n        <strong>NF4 quantisation.</strong> All experiments use 4-bit NF4 quantisation. The refusal\n        direction and abliteration behaviour may differ at full precision or other quantisation levels.\n      </li>\n      <li>\n        <strong>Single Heretic configuration.</strong> The abliteration uses a single Heretic\n        configuration per model (116 TPE trials, default hyperparameter ranges). A more exhaustive\n        search might yield different results.\n      </li>\n    </ul>\n  </section>\n\n  <!-- ============ CODE ARTIFACTS ============ -->\n  <section class=\"code-artifacts\"
